### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **49** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/currency.mdx`  _(via MMK (symbol, a field of const object STANDARD_UNIT_NAMES; a field of const object STANDARD_UNIT_NAME_TRANSLATIONS))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/units.mdx`  _(via KGM (symbol, a field of const object STANDARD_UNIT_NAMES; a field of const object STANDARD_UNIT_NAME_TRANSLATIONS), MTR (symbol, a field of const object STANDARD_UNIT_NAMES; a field of const object STANDARD_UNIT_NAME_TRANSLATIONS))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via KGM (symbol, a field of const object STANDARD_UNIT_NAMES; a field of const object STANDARD_UNIT_NAME_TRANSLATIONS))_
- `content/docs/frontend/fields.mdx`  _(via KGM (symbol, a field of const object STANDARD_UNIT_NAMES; a field of const object STANDARD_UNIT_NAME_TRANSLATIONS), STANDARD_UNIT_NAMES (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/protocol/diagram.mdx`  _(via SEC (symbol, a field of const object STANDARD_UNIT_NAMES; a field of const object STANDARD_UNIT_NAME_TRANSLATIONS))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4925039a7558d6477323eeef7b1b16d89da01cc3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `58db4ead191a0f528b47adbfe79e4756b86ff60c` — the merge of head `37fca77eee7be2df4c6073dac7c5d9a628ca6552` into base `4925039a7558d6477323eeef7b1b16d89da01cc3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 58db4ead191a0f528b47adbfe79e4756b86ff60c && git checkout 58db4ead191a0f528b47adbfe79e4756b86ff60c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4925039a7558d6477323eeef7b1b16d89da01cc3 37fca77eee7be2df4c6073dac7c5d9a628ca6552 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4925039a7558d6477323eeef7b1b16d89da01cc3 && git merge --no-ff 37fca77eee7be2df4c6073dac7c5d9a628ca6552

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4925039a7558d6477323eeef7b1b16d89da01cc3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4925039a7558d6477323eeef7b1b16d89da01cc3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Final head: `7b7017e7be095a8b64cd73bbe0273cf94105c147`. All 70 check-runs on it have completed: 61 success and 9 skipped (opt-in or path-selected lanes). None failed, and the PR merges cleanly. Since the PR opened, four CI fixes landed: the spec `export-origins` baseline gained the two new exports; the quantity form test loads `@object-ui/react-runtime` at collection (the test-source alias gate); the test regexes escape their NBSPs; and `unitConfig` is now declared on `FormFieldSchema` (and `FormField`) beside `currencyConfig`, because the number widget reads it (the form-field channel census). Ready for L1 and the seat's contract review (Clause-② yes, widening: two added `@objectstack/spec` exports, `STANDARD_UNIT_NAMES` and `standardUnitName`, plus the optional `unitConfig` key on the ui form field face).

**Where the per-locale names are served (measured).** The platform-objects translation bundles, in their flat `messages` map, with single-segment keys `standardUnit<CODE>`. The keys are not dotted, because `FileI18nAdapter.resolveKey` splits on `.` and walks the parts as nesting. The UI reads `app.messages.standardUnit<CODE>`, since the console lays the bundles under `app`. When no name is served, it falls back to the spec English base.

## ADR-0158 amendment text (for the ADR owner; `docs/adr/**` is outside this card's fence)

> **Open item 6, settled (ruling A, objectstack#35490).** A quantity's display rounds at render, half away from zero, at a fixed width. The width is `min(the unit's decimal places, the field's scale)`, per L4. A field with no `scale` takes the unit's places. A unit with no places uses the field's own width. Only the display rounds. The stored value, a total (summed exact, then formatted), an export, the API and MCP keep the exact value. No marker is shown when the display hides places.
>
> **Open item 10, the row read.** A standard code's decimal places come from the `sys_standard_unit_setting` row whose `organization_id` matches the record's organization. A record with no organization stamp matches a row with none. A record that carries no organization takes the row only when exactly one candidate exists. An org unit's places and label come from its own `sys_unit` row, chosen the same way.
>
> **L1 / Open item 11, the bare code.** A retired org unit, an unknown code, and a reader who may not read `sys_unit` (an external member) see the bare code. They never see an error.
>
> **L2 (2A), where names live.** The English base name of every standard code is `STANDARD_UNIT_NAMES` in `@objectstack/spec`. The platform serves each locale's name as `messages.standardUnit<CODE>` in the platform-objects bundles. The English bundle copies the spec base. A reader whose locale has no served name sees the English base.
>
> **Follow-up item (not built).** Add an optional per-unit write-time over-precision refusal. A unit could declare that a value carrying more places than its decimal places is refused at write. It is refused and never rounded. This stays within L4: the field's `scale` remains the ceiling, and nothing rounds at write.

Deferred: platform-catalog row → #37431 (`skills/**` fence).

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7b7017e7be095a8b64cd73bbe0273cf94105c147`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/standard-units.ts + packages/spec/src/data/standard-units.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/standard-unit-names.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/standard-unit-names.test.ts, the eleven platform-objects bundle files (en, zh-CN, zh-Hant, ja-JP, ko, de, fr, es-ES, pt-BR, ru, ar), ui/packages/core/src/utils/unit-display.ts, ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/useQuantityUnit.ts, ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/quantity-format.ts, ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/QuantityText.tsx, ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/NumberField.tsx, ui/packages/fields/src/index.tsx, ui/packages/types/src/form.ts, ui/packages/types/src/zod/form.zod.ts, ui/packages/types/src/field-types.ts, ui/packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/objectGridRowLoad.ts, ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/objectGridGenerateColumns.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/RelatedList.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/RecordDetailPanel.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/fieldEnrichment.ts

Inputs read: card #35490 (body and all six comments), the PR body, the 44-file net diff against `main`, the 70 check-runs on the head (61 success, 9 skipped, none failed), and final-head comment 7185000835. Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed: ADR-0158 on `main`, `file-i18n-adapter.ts#resolveKey`, `spec-translations.ts#transformSpecTranslations`, `setup.translation.ts`, `source-hash.ts`, `field-scale.ts`, `number-display.ts`, `useColumnSummary.ts`, `strict-authoring-face.ts`, `TextField.tsx`, the two `sys_*` unit objects.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`@objectstack/spec` public surface: two added exports, nothing removed. Right.** `STANDARD_UNIT_NAMES` (const) and `standardUnitName` (function), both from `src/data/standard-units.ts`. `api-surface/data.json` and `export-origins/data.json` each gain exactly those two rows and lose none, which matches the source diff.
- **`@object-ui/types`: one optional key, `unitConfig`, on `FormField` and `FormFieldSchema`, and on `NumberFieldMetadata` and `TextFieldMetadata`. Right as a widening.** Each is `SpecField['unitConfig']` by reference, beside `currencyConfig`. `FormField` has no index signature, so the TypeScript side is purely additive. `FormFieldSchema` is a `looseObject`, and the strict authoring face (`StrictAnyComponentSchema`, what `objectui validate` runs) is derived from it, so a hand-authored form field may now write `unitConfig` where the strict face refused it before. The PR adds the key to the test's "authorable key surface" list itself. See S3 for what that implies for the changeset.
- **`@objectstack/platform-objects`: each of the eleven bundles gains a `messages` group of 41 keys. Right.** `messages` is not in `HAND_AUTHORED_SECTIONS` or `GENERATED_SECTIONS`, so `withSourceFallback` serves it verbatim. No bundle had a `messages` group before, so nothing is overwritten.
- **`@object-ui/core` and `@object-ui/fields`: new exports only** (`unit-display.ts`; `QuantityText`, `UnitCodeText`, `formatQuantity`, `quantityDisplayPlaces`, `useQuantityUnit`, `useStandardUnitLabel`, `readUnitCatalog`). `CellRendererProps` and the widget props are read, not changed.
- **Accept sets on the server: none moved.** No object definition, route, or engine file is in the diff.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening) — accurate for `@objectstack/spec` and for `@object-ui/types`. No export, key or accepted value is removed anywhere in the diff.

- `@objectstack/spec: patch` with `Metadata-protocol: none` is right for the spec: two exports are not something a metadata author writes, and AGENTS.md's Post-Task rule 3 ships a non-protocol widening as `patch`.
- `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@object-ui/core`, `fields`, `components`, `plugin-grid`, `plugin-list`, `plugin-detail` at `patch`: right, on the same rule.
- **S3 (should-fix) — the changeset and the PR body declare `Metadata-protocol: none`, and `@object-ui/types` ships at `patch`, but the diff adds an authorable key.** `unitConfig` is newly declared on `FormFieldSchema`, joins `DECLARED_KEYS` ("the AUTHORABLE key surface of `FormField`") in `form-field-zod-coverage.test.ts`, and is therefore newly accepted by `objectui validate` on a hand-authored form field. AGENTS.md: "a new key, accepted value or metadata type is `added`", and "a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves". The precedents for this exact move shipped as minor: `scale` and `currencyConfig` on the same face (18d7b48, objectui#11070) and the objectui#12130 keys (c0c2f79, 0665c3b). The claim said `none` "re-states from its diff"; the key arrived with the fourth CI fix and the line was not re-stated. The changeset body also never names the new form-field key; only comment 7185000835 does. Fix: `Metadata-protocol: added` in the changeset and the PR body, `@object-ui/types: minor`, and one sentence in the changeset body naming `unitConfig` on `FormField` / `FormFieldSchema`.
- N1 (nit) — the tolerant face tightens on values: a form field carrying a malformed `unitConfig` passed `FormFieldSchema` as an unknown key and is now refused by the spec's `UnitConfigSchema`. Nothing read the key before, and the identical move for the objectui#11070 keys was declared a widening ("the tolerant face narrows on their values"), so the `Clause-②` arm stands. The changeset could say it in one line.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **OI6 = A, round at render: held.** The only rounding in the diff is `quantityFractionDigits` in `quantity-format.ts`, fed to `Intl.NumberFormat` (default `halfExpand`) through `formatDisplayNumber`, whose `scale` option decides grouping only. No path writes a rounded value: the edited box still emits `Number(val)`, no `step` or blur rule reads the unit's places, and no footer, export, API or engine file is touched. `hidden` is computed and nothing draws it.
- **Unit names = spec base + server-side translation: held.** The English base is in the spec; the ten translations are in `standard-unit-names.ts`; the `en` bundle is built from `STANDARD_UNIT_NAMES`, not re-typed. No `ui/packages/i18n` file is in the net diff and no unit name string exists anywhere under `ui/`. The UI imports only `standardUnitName` as the fallback.
- **Keys and the dot split: held in code.** `standardUnitMessageKey` returns `standardUnit` + code, the codes are `[A-Z0-9]+`, and the pin test asserts no key holds a dot. `resolveKey` then walks `messages` → `standardUnitKGM`. On the client `transformSpecTranslations` copies `messages` under `app`, so `app.messages.standardUnitKGM` is three intended segments. The one dotted spelling left is in the spec jsdoc: S1.
- **Note 7180167601, items 1 and 2: answered.** `pickRowForOrganization` picks the row of the record's organization, never the first; `quantityDisplayPlaces` is `min(unit places, scale)`.
- **Note 7180167601, item 3 (platform-catalog row): deferred honestly.** #37431 exists, is open (`pm:queue`, p3, `domain:skills`), and carries exactly this row with the reason (it regenerates a `skills/**` file).
- **Comment 7030066814 (external member): answered and pinned.** Each table is read on its own; a refused read leaves that table unread and the code bare. Pinned in `quantityDisplay-35490.test.tsx`.
- **S2 (should-fix) — Open item 8's picker is neither built nor escalated, and `Fixes #35490` closes the card that carries it.** The card body lists "OI8, ruled A: a standalone unit field also renders with its label and gets the picker". The ruling record 7008524997 on #35339 holds the accepted consequence 「有下拉」, and ADR-0158 Open item 8 on `main` names #35490 "the picker card". The diff draws the label in cells (`UnitCodeText` through `TextCellRenderer`) and stops there: no unit dropdown exists for a `code` field or for a quantity's `unitField`, and on the form face `TextField` does not read `unitConfig` at all, so a `code` field in a form shows the bare code even read-only. The PR body, its acceptance notes and the amendment text in 7185000835 do not mention the picker. Close it by building it, or by filing the picker card and naming it in the PR body and the amendment text, with `Part of` in place of `Fixes` if the card must stay open. The `FormField.unitConfig` jsdoc and the `form.zod.ts` comment also describe `unitMode: 'code'` on a `text` field; on this face nothing reads that mode yet, and the same note should say so.
- **Write-time over-precision refusal: honest, not owed now.** L4 forbids rounding at write and R1 has four members; a refusal is a new rule that needs a new unit key and its own ruling. It is correctly marked "not built". N3 (nit): it has no card, so once the text is filed on #37245 the ADR would hold a promise nobody owns. File the card, or write it as a numbered Open item that names its owner, when the row is added.
- **SQL push-down: no finding.** The one new read is `readUnitCatalog`: both unit tables, whole, once per adapter per session, joined to rows in the client by code and organization. A reason is given in the code (short reference lists, the `homeAmountPreview` precedent), and `$expand` cannot serve the join because a record stores the code, not an id (U4). The projection changes add columns to an existing `$select`; none adds a query. N4 (nit): a failed read is cached as "unread" for the session, so a transient error leaves codes bare until reload; `$top: 2000` truncates in silence; and the read does not send `$count: false`, so each table also costs a `count(*)`.
- **The four surfaces.** Grid: `unitConfig` copied on all three column paths, `unitField` and `organization_id` added to the projection through the same two gates as the currency harvest. List: the same reads through `addPredicateField`. Detail: `ENRICHED_FIELD_METADATA_KEYS`, `buildRecordDetailFields` and `RelatedList` (projection and cell bag). Form: `number` joins the live-record widgets. One resolver and one formatter serve all four, so a quantity cannot draw differently between them. A form's values may lack `organization_id`; the resolver then answers only when exactly one row exists, which is the safe direction and is what the amendment says. The gap between surfaces is the `code` field on the form face, under S2.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/standard-units.ts` (hits).**

- The table holds against its ruling and its consumers. 41 names, keyed and ordered as `STANDARD_UNITS`; frozen; `standardUnitName` is an own-property lookup in exact uppercase, as `standardUnitOf` is. The pin test fails a code added without a name. H87 is "piece" (U2). The first consumers read it as designed: the `en` bundle copies it and `useStandardUnitLabel` falls back to it.
- **S1 (should-fix) — the jsdoc on `STANDARD_UNIT_NAMES` states the key the ruling's implementation rejected.** It says each locale's name is served from "the platform translation bundles' `messages`, keyed `units.standard.` plus the code" (the code in angle brackets in the source). The served key is `standardUnit` plus the code, e.g. `standardUnitKGM`. The dotted form is exactly the one `resolveKey` would split into three nested segments and fail to find, and this sentence is the published contract a server-side reader (the export or MCP reader the same comment names) would follow. Every other mention in the diff uses the right key. Fix: name the single-segment key there (`standardUnit` followed by the code, e.g. `standardUnitKGM`).

**Implementing files.**

- `unit-display.ts`: agrees with ADR-0158 U4, L1, L4 and Open item 10 and with the amendment text. A retired row, a missing row and an unread table all resolve to the bare code with no places. Decimal places outside 0..12 are ignored. Codes are never trimmed or case-folded.
- `quantity-format.ts`: agrees with the OI6 ruling and with L4. `resolveFieldScale` returns `undefined` for a `number` field with no `scale`, so "a field with no `scale` takes the unit's places" is true in code.
- `useQuantityUnit.ts`: agrees. `t(key, { defaultValue: base })` returns the served name or the spec base on both the provider and the provider-less path.
- `standard-unit-names.ts` and the bundles: agree. The locale set is pinned to the bundle set, and every locale to exactly the 41 codes.
- `form.ts`, `form.zod.ts`, `field-types.ts`: agree with the spec member they reference; see S2 for the `code` mode on the form face and S3 for the changeset.
- Grid, list, detail and form wiring: agree with the contract, as set out under ③.

**The ADR-0158 amendment text in 7185000835 against the code.** Consistent on Open item 6, L1 / Open item 11, L2 and the follow-up item. Two wordings to tighten when the row is filed on #37245 (no row for this PR is there yet, which is expected before landing):

- N2 (nit) — Open item 10: "a record with no organization stamp" and "a record that carries no organization" read as the same case and are two in code: `organization_id` present and empty matches a row with none; `organization_id` not read at all takes a row only when exactly one exists. Open item 6: "a total (summed exact, then formatted)" is true, but a reader may take it to mean the unit's width. The footer is untouched by this diff: it draws a fixed-mode quantity's sum at the field's own width with no unit, and `main` already withholds the sum of a record-mode quantity.

Other nits:

- N5 (nit) — `messages` sits outside the staleness mechanism, so a later edit of a spec English name leaves the ten translations served with no flag. The pin test checks key sets only.
- N6 (nit) — tests: no negative half case (`-1.5` at 0 places) pins "away from zero"; `expect(value).toBe(1.5)` on a number primitive cannot fail; nothing pins a footer or an export of a quantity as exact (they are exact because the diff does not touch them).

Findings open on this head: S1, S2, S3. No must-fix. Each should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; S2 and the PR-body half of S3 can close on the prose faces, S1 and the changeset half of S3 move the head.

## 席位核对

Head-sha: `7b7017e7be095a8b64cd73bbe0273cf94105c147`
**REWORK** — L1, seat repo:objectstack#5: contract record 7185313489 (schema face, `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`) reads PASS, with three should-fix findings and no must-fix. Both maintainer rulings hold in the tree (OI6 = round at render, display path only; spec English base names plus server-side single-segment `standardUnit<CODE>` keys). S1–S3 close before ACCEPT.

1. **Shape**: open draft against `main`, 44 files (+2172/−42), `Fixes #35490`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. Not governed, 2214 lines ≤ 3000. `l1-face` is clean. Check-runs: 70 completed, 61 success, 9 skipped, 0 failed.
2. **Premise**: there is no rounding on any stored, total, export or API path. No unit name table remains under `ui/`, and the pin test refuses a dotted key. The grid/list/detail/form relay is consistent for quantities. The platform-catalog row is on #37431 (open). There is no SQL push-down question: the catalog read is whole-table, because a record stores a code, not an id.
3. **Owed before ACCEPT**:
   - **S1.** The `STANDARD_UNIT_NAMES` jsdoc in `packages/spec/src/data/standard-units.ts` still says `units.standard.CODE`. That is the dotted form `FileI18nAdapter` splits. Correct it to `standardUnit<CODE>`.
   - **S2.** ADR-0158 Open item 8's picker (card body; ruling 7008524997 「有下拉」) is neither built nor carried, and on the form face a `code` field shows the bare code. Either build it, or file a picker card under #35490 and change the PR to `Part of #35490`, naming that card in the body and the amendment text. `Fixes #35490` must not close the card that carries it.
   - **S3.** `unitConfig` is a new authorable key on `FormFieldSchema`. `objectui validate` newly accepts it, and the PR adds it to the authorable-key list itself. So per AGENTS.md: `Metadata-protocol: added`, `@object-ui/types` at `minor` (precedent: `scale` / `currencyConfig`, 18d7b48), and the changeset names the key. Fix it on both carriers.
   The same reviewer reads the delta.
4. **Accepted deviations** (nits, record only, unless cheap in the same push):
   - N1: the tolerant face now refuses a malformed `unitConfig` (objectui#11070 precedent).
   - N2: two wording points in the amendment (organization stamp vs no organization; the footer total is formatted at the field's width with no unit).
   - N4: the catalog read caches a failure for the session, truncates silently at `$top: 2000` and sends no `$count: false`.
   - N5: `messages` sits outside the staleness mechanism.
   - N6: no negative half case, one vacuous `toBe(1.5)`, and no pin for footer or export exactness.
5. **Out of scope and where it went**:
   - N3: the write-time over-precision refusal is honestly not built and not owed now. It needs a card or a named owner when the row goes on #37245.
   - N4 and N5 can share one follow-up card, `review follow-ups of PR #37449`, filed by the area.
6. **Landing terms**: ungoverned. Owed: S1–S3 closed, a same-head at-tier delta PASS, and an **ACCEPT**. Then the area lands it, and after landing files the ADR-0158 amendment row on #37245.
